raw_text:
Here is a concise, self-contained 12-week program summary you can hand to the client or use as a quick-reference guide. It combines the strength plan, cardio, anti-inflammatory nutrition, core/abs work, sleep/recovery protocol, and 1RM testing in Week 12. The structure stays 4 lifting days per week with two cardio sessions and integrated core work, while emphasizing spinal safety for a history of L4–L5 disc herniation.

Overall structure
- Frequency: 4 resistance days per week (Lower A, Upper A, Lower B, Upper B) + 2 cardio days + optional mobility/active recovery
- Phases:
  - Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Foundation, movement quality, bracing, and tolerable loads
  - Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Increased intensity and volume with safe progressions
  - Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Higher intensity, strength and durability emphasis, with Week 12 testing
- Core/abs work: 2–3 short core sessions per week (anti-rotation/anti-extension focus)
- 1RM testing: Week 12, integrated safely for hip hinge, press, and row patterns

Weekly template (core layout)
- Monday: Lower A (hip-dominant)
- Tuesday: Upper A (push/pull)
- Wednesday: Rest or mobility
- Thursday: Lower B (quad emphasis)
- Friday: Upper B (pull/press with scapular work)
- Saturday: Cardio session 1
- Sunday: Cardio session 2 or mobility/active recovery

Phase I: Foundation and movement quality (Weeks 1–4)
Goals: Technique, neutral spine bracing, base strength, and tolerance to loading with safe patterns.
- Lower A (Hip-dominant)
  - Goblet Squat or Front Foot Elevated Split Squat: 3x8–10
  - Romanian Deadlift (DB or light barbell): 3x8
  - Hip Thrust (bodyweight to moderate load): 3x10
  - Pallof Press: 3x10 per side
  - Carry (Farmer’s or Suitcase): 3x30–40s
  - Core: Plank 3x30–40s; Side Plank 3x20–30s per side
- Upper A (Push/Pull)
  - DB Bench or Incline DB Press: 3x8–10
  - Seated Cable Row or DB Row: 3x8–10
  - Overhead Press (light): 3x8
  - Lat Pulldown (neutral grip): 3x8–10
  - Face Pulls: 3x12–15
  - Pallof Press or Dead Bug: 3x8–10 per side
- Cardio: 2x20–25 minutes (easy to moderate, RPE 5–7)
- Nutrition: Anti-inflammatory framework; protein 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day; hydration 2.2–3 L/day; emphasize omega-3s, vegetables, lean proteins, whole grains
- Sleep/Recovery: Target 7–9 hours; consistent schedule

Phase II: Build strength and tolerance (Weeks 5–8)
Goals: Higher intensity with safe patterns; progressive overload on main lifts; maintain anti-rotation/anti-extension core work
- Week 5–6
  - Lower A (Lower with heavier loading)
    - Barbell Hip Thrust or Dumbbell Hip Thrust: 4x6–8
    - Bulgarian Split Squat: 3x6–8 per leg
    - Trap Bar/Hex Deadlift or Sumo Deadlift (light-to-moderate): 3x5–6
    - Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift: 2–3x6–8 per leg
    - Pallof Press: 3x10–12 per side
    - Anti-extension core: Dead Bug 3x12
  - Upper A (Push/Pull intensified)
    - Barbell Bench or DB Bench: 4x6–8
    - Barbell Rows or T-Bar Rows: 3x6–8
    - Overhead Press (DB or Barbell): 3x6–8
    - Pull-Ups/Assisted or Lat Pulldown: 3x8–10
    - Face Pulls: 3x12–15
    - Farmer’s Carry: 3x40–60s
- Week 7–8
  - Lower B (Quad emphasis)
    - Barbell Back Squat (tolerated) or Front Squat: 4x5–6
    - Front Squat or Goblet Front Squat: 3x6–8
    - Romanian Deadlift: 3x6–8
    - Bulgarian Split Squat or Step-Ups: 3x6–8 per leg
    - Pallof Press: 3x12 per side
    - Core stability circuit: 2 rounds (Plank 40s, Dead Bug 12 reps per side)
  - Upper B (Push/Pull)
    - Floor Press or Bench Press: 4x5–6
    - Pendlay Rows or Barbell Rows: 3x6–8
    - Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press: 3x6–8
    - Lat Pulldown: 3x8–10
    - Face Pulls: 3x12–15
    - Farmer’s Carry or Suitcase Carry: 3x40–60s
- Cardio: 2x25–30 minutes, one day with light intervals optional; maintain RPE 5–7
- Core: Continue 2–3 sessions/week; emphasize anti-rotation

Phase III: Strength and durability (Weeks 9–12)
Goals: Peak strength while maintaining technique; safer higher-intensity work; plan for Week 12 1RM testing
- Week 9–10
  - Lower A
    - Barbell Hip Thrust: 4x5–6
    - Back Squat (if tolerated) or Front Squat: 3x5–6
    - Romanian Deadlift: 3x5–6
    - Bulgarian Split Squat: 3x6 per leg
    - Pallof Press: 3x12 per side
    - Core: 3x40s plank variations
  - Upper A
    - Bench or Floor Press: 4x5–6
    - Pendlay Rows or Barbell Rows: 3x5–6
    - Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press: 3x5–6
    - Pull-Ups/Lat Pulldown: 3x6–8
    - Face Pulls: 3x12–15
    - Carry: 3x60s
- Week 11
  - Lower B: 4x4–6 on hip-dominated lifts; Front Squat 3x5–6; Romanian Deadlift 3x5–6
  - Upper B: 4x5–6 on press and 3x6–8 rows
  - Core/Abs: maintenance 5–12 minutes total
- Week 12 (1RM testing week; reduced volume)
  - Day A: Hip hinge-based testing
    - Warm-up progression; 1–2 heavy singles on Hip Thrust or preferred hip hinge
    - Record 1RM where safely completed with good form and no pain
  - Day B: Press pattern testing
    - Floor Press or Incline DB Press first; ramp to single
    - Record 1RM if tolerated
  - Day C (optional): Rowing pull test (if planned)
  - Deload if needed: After testing, reduce volume 40–50% for 1–2 days if fatigue is high
- Cardio: Maintain 2x per week; adjust based on energy from testing

1RM testing protocol in Week 12 (summary)
- Lifts tested: 1 of hip hinge (hip thrust or RDL), 1 press (floor or incline), 1 row (barbell or Pendlay)
- Warm-up: 5–10 min light cardio, mobility; then progressive warm-ups (e.g., 5–10–15–20–30% of anticipated max; 1–2 reps at 40–70%, then attempts)
- Attempts: 3–5 attempts per lift, with 3–5 min rest between attempts
- Success criteria: controlled form, pain-free, full range; stop if form falters
- If pain or symptoms occur, revert to last successful set and schedule re-test later

Nutrition (anti-inflammatory) overview across 12 weeks
- Protein target: 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day
- Carbs: 3–5 g/kg/day (adjust up on high volume days)
- Fats: fill remaining calories with healthy fats
- Daily focus: fatty fish 2–3x/week, omega-3s, berries, leafy greens, olive oil, nuts/seeds, legumes
- Hydration: 2.2–3 L/day
- Recovery nutrition: protein + carbs within 1–2 hours post-workout
- Supplements (optional): omega-3 1–2 g/day, vitamin D as needed, magnesium if sleep is poor, turmeric/curcumin 500–1000 mg/day with pepper
- Sleep and recovery aligned with nutrition for muscle repair

Sleep and recovery protocol (summary)
- Sleep 7–9 hours per night; consistent bedtime/wake time
- Pre-sleep routine: dim lights, light mobility/breathing
- Sleep environment: cool, dark, quiet
- Daytime: morning light, caffeine cutoff by 2–3 pm, limited naps
- Recovery: daily 5–10 min mobility; 2–3 days/week 5–10 min dedicated breathing/bracing practice; deload weeks (Weeks 4 and 8)
- Weekly check-ins: track sleep hours and quality; adjust caffeine, bedtime, and workload as needed

Cardio (integrated)
- 2 sessions per week; 20–30 minutes per session; steady-state at RPE 5–7
- Low-to-moderate impact modalities
- Progression: Weeks 1–4 2x20–25 min; Weeks 5–12 2x25–30 min
- Optional light intervals if tolerable (20–60 seconds at RPE 7 with equal easy pace)

Abs/core (integrated)
- Core work focused on anti-extension/anti-rotation
- 2–3 sessions per week; 5–12 minutes total per session
- Progression: from basic planks/dead bugs/pallof presses to heavier braced variations as tolerated

Safety considerations
- Spine neutral, bracing, diaphragmatic breathing at all times
- No heavy spinal flexion exercises; substitute with anti-rotation/anti-extension core work
- Any back pain or radicular symptoms require immediate regression and clinician consultation
- If any lift causes pain, reduce load, range, or switch to a safer variation

Data collection and next steps
- Record weekly training numbers (loads, reps, RPE), sleep hours/quality, and recovery notes
- After Week 12 testing, use 1RM data to calibrate the next 8–12 week plan with progressive overload targets
- If desired, I can output a detailed week-by-week table with exact exercise choices, sets/reps, progression targets, and a grocery/meal plan aligned to Week 1–12
